#Unsupervised Learning

##Load the cost of living data
```{r}
cost_of_living_df <- read_csv("Desktop/machine learning cw/datasets/cost-of-living_v2.csv")
View(cost_of_living_df)
summary(cost_of_living_df)
```

##Ensure all feature columns are numeric
```{r}
id_cols <- c("city", "country")
num_cols <- setdiff(colnames(cost_of_living_df), id_cols)

for (col in num_cols) {
  cost_of_living_df[[col]] <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(cost_of_living_df[[col]]))
}
```

##Check for missing values
```{r}
sum(is.na(cost_of_living_df))
```

##Drop columns with more than 30% missing values
```{r}
missing_pct <- colSums(is.na(cost_of_living_df[, num_cols])) / nrow(cost_of_living_df) * 100
drop_cols   <- names(missing_pct[missing_pct > 30])
print(drop_cols)

cost_of_living_df <- cost_of_living_df %>% select(-all_of(drop_cols))
num_cols <- setdiff(colnames(cost_of_living_df), id_cols)
```

##Impute missing values with column median
```{r}
cost_of_living_df <- cost_of_living_df %>% mutate(across(all_of(num_cols),
                    ~ ifelse(is.na(.), median(., na.rm=TRUE), .)))
```

##Check for duplicate rows
```{r}
sum(duplicated(cost_of_living_df))
```

##Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
```{r}
#Select 9 variables to plot
vars_9 <- c("x1","x23","x24","x31","x33","x36","x45","x48","x54")
labels_9 <- c("Restaurant meal", "Water(1.5L)", "Wine (bottle)",
              "Taxi (1km)", "Gasoline (1L)", "Utilities",
              "Dress", "1 Bedroom Apartment Rent (City)", "Monthly Net Salary")
plot_data <- cost_of_living_df %>%
              select(all_of(vars_9)) %>%
              setNames(labels_9) %>%        
              pivot_longer(everything(),
                  names_to  = "Variable",
                  values_to = "Value") %>%
              filter(!is.na(Value))
#Generate distribution plots
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Value)) +
     geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue",
                    colour = "white", alpha = 0.85) +
     facet_wrap(~ Variable,
                scales = "free",     
                ncol   = 3) +        
     labs(title = "Distribution Plot",
          x     = "Price (USD)",
          y     = "Count") +
     theme_minimal() +
     theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 5, face = "bold"),
           axis.text  = element_text(size = 5))

#Most and least expensive cities to rent a 1 bedroom apartment in the city centre
rent_onebed_city_col <- "x48"
top10_expensive <- cost_of_living_df %>% 
                    arrange(desc(.data[[rent_onebed_city_col]])) %>% 
                    select(city, country, all_of(rent_onebed_city_col)) %>% 
                    head(10)

top10_cheapest <- cost_of_living_df %>% 
                  arrange(.data[[rent_onebed_city_col]]) %>%
                  select(city, country, all_of(rent_onebed_city_col)) %>% 
                  head(10)

#Correlation heatmap of price variables
#Select key columns by catergories
key_cols <- c("x1",     # Food - restaurant meal
              "x6",     # Beverage - coffee
              "x16",    # Food - fruits
              "x23",    # Beverage - water
              "x24",    # Beverage - alcohol
              "x31",    # Transport - taxi 
              "x33",    # Transport - gasoline
              "x34",    # Transport - Volkswagen Golf 1.4 90KW Trendline or equivalent new car
              "x36",    # Bills - apartment
              "x39",    # Bills - fitness club
              "x45",    # Clothing - dress
              "x48",    # Housing - 1 bedroom apartment in the city center
              "x54")    # Wages - monthly net salary
corr_matrix  <- cor(cost_of_living_df[, key_cols], use = "complete.obs")

#Plot the correlation heatmap
corrplot(corr_matrix,
         method  = "color",
         type    = "upper",
         tl.cex  = 0.8,
         tl.col  = "black",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex  = 0.55,
         title   = "Correlation Heatmap — Key Price Variables",
         mar     = c(0, 0, 2, 0)
)
```

##Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
```{r}
#Create new dataframe with price columns only and scale it
prices_df <- cost_of_living_df[, num_cols]
prices_df_scaled <- scale(prices_df)
pca_result <- prcomp(prices_df_scaled, center=FALSE, scale.=FALSE)

#Generate scree plotto visualise variance explained per component
scree_plot <- fviz_eig(pca_result, addlabels=TRUE, ncp=15, barfill="blue", barcolor="white", main="PCA scree plot — variance explained per component")
print(scree_plot)

#Compute cumulative variance explained
cumulative_var <- cumsum(pca_result$sdev^2 / sum(pca_result$sdev^2)) * 100

#Create new data frame for plotting scree plot
scree2_df <- data.frame(PC = seq_along(cumulative_var), Variance = cumulative_var)

#Generate scree plot to visualise cumulative variance explained
ggplot(scree2_df, aes(x = PC, y = Variance)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue") +
  geom_point(size = 1, color = "blue") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, max(scree2_df$PC), by = 5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10),  # <-- change to 100
                     limits = c(0, 100)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  ggtitle("Scree Plot: Cumulative Variance Explained") +
  xlab("Number of Components") +
  ylab("Cumulative Variance Explained (%)")

#How many components explain at least 80% of variance?
n_comp_80 <- which(cumulative_var >= 80)[1]

#Top contributing variables to PC1 and PC2
loadings_df <- as.data.frame(pca_result$rotation[, 1:4])
loadings_df$Feature <- rownames(loadings_df)

print(loadings_df %>%
        arrange(desc(abs(PC1))) %>%
        select(Feature, PC1) %>%
        head(10))

print(loadings_df %>%
        arrange(desc(abs(PC2))) %>%
        select(Feature, PC2) %>%
        head(10))
```

##K-Means Clustering
```{r}
set.seed(12)
#Find optimal k using elbow method
wss_values <- sapply(1:12, function(k) {
  kmeans(prices_df_scaled, centers=k, nstart=25, iter.max=200)$tot.withinss
})

plot(1:12, wss_values,
      type = "b", pch = 19, cex = 1.2,
      col  = "blue",
      xlab = "Number of clusters (k)",
      ylab = "Total within-cluster sum of squares (WSS)",
      main = "Elbow method — optimal number of clusters")
abline(v = which(diff(diff(wss_values)) == max(diff(diff(wss_values)))) + 1, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)

#Find optimal k using silhouette method
fviz_nbclust(prices_df_scaled,
              kmeans,
              method = "silhouette",
              k.max  = 12,
              nstart = 25) +
              labs(title = "Silhouette method — optimal number of clusters")

#Set the number of clusters
optimal_k <- 2

#Apply K-Means Clustering
set.seed(12)
kmeans_result  <- kmeans(prices_df_scaled, centers = optimal_k, nstart = 50, iter.max = 300)
cost_of_living_df$Cluster <- as.factor(kmeans_result$cluster)
print(table(cost_of_living_df$Cluster))

#Visualise clusters on PCA plot
fviz_cluster(kmeans_result,
              data         = prices_df_scaled,
              geom         = "point",
              ellipse.type = "convex",
              palette      = c("green", "blue",
                               "red", "purple",
                               "orange")[1:optimal_k],
              alpha        = 0.5,
              ggtheme      = theme_minimal(),
              main         = paste0("K-Means Clusters (k = ",
                                    optimal_k, ") — PCA Projection"))

#Box plot of monthly net salary by cluster
ggplot(cost_of_living_df, aes(x = Cluster, y = x54, fill = Cluster)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.85, outlier.size = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("green", "blue")[1:optimal_k]) +
  labs(title = "Monthly Net Salary by cluster",
       x = "Cluster", y = "Monthly Net Salary (USD)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

##Hierarchical CLustering
```{r}
#Use a sample of 300 cities as using all 4700 is not viable for reading dendrogram
samplecities  <- sample(1:nrow(prices_df_scaled), 300)
hc_data     <- prices_df_scaled[samplecities, ]
hc_labels   <- cost_of_living_df$city[samplecities]

#Compute Euclidean distance
hc_dist   <- dist(hc_data, method = "euclidean")

#Use Ward's method
hc_result <- hclust(hc_dist, method = "ward.D2")

#Generate dendrogram
plot(hc_result,
     labels = FALSE,
     hang = -1,
     cex = 0.6,
     main = paste0("Hierarchical Clustering Dendrogram\n",
                     "(random sample of 300 cities)"),
     xlab = "Cities",
     sub = "")

rect.hclust(hc_result,
             k = optimal_k,
             border = c("green", "blue")[1:optimal_k])

#Cut the tree
hc_clusters <- cutree(hc_result, k = optimal_k)
print(table(hc_clusters))

#Calculate the difference between cluster medians for each variable
cluster_diff <- cost_of_living_df %>%
  group_by(Cluster) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(key_cols),
                   ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-Cluster,
               names_to  = "Variable",
               values_to = "Median") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from  = Cluster,
              values_from = Median) %>%
  mutate(Difference = abs(`1` - `2`)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Difference))

print(head(cluster_diff, 10))
```

#Regression

#Install packages
```{r}
install.packages("caret")
install.packages("glmnet")
install.packages("rpart")
install.packages("rpart.plot")
install.packages("randomForest")
install.packages("ranger")
``` 
##Load libraries
```{r}
library(caret)
library(glmnet)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(randomForest)
library(ranger)

set.seed(12)
```

##Load hotel reservations dataset
```{r}
Hotel_Reservations <- read_csv("Desktop/machine learning cw/datasets/Hotel Reservations.csv")
View(Hotel_Reservations)
```

##Check for missing values
```{r}
any(is.na(Hotel_Reservations))
```

##Preprocessing
```{r}
#Remove identifier columns
hotel_df <- Hotel_Reservations %>% 
            select(-any_of(c("Booking_ID")))
 
#Convert categorical variables into factors
hotel_df <- hotel_df %>%
            mutate(across(c(type_of_meal_plan, room_type_reserved,
                  market_segment_type, booking_status,
                  repeated_guest, required_car_parking_space),
                  as.factor))

#Remove rows where avg_price_per_room is 0
hotel_df <- hotel_df %>%
            filter(!is.na(avg_price_per_room), avg_price_per_room > 0)
```

##Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
```{r}
#Distribution of room prices
ggplot(hotel_df, aes(x = avg_price_per_room)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "blue", colour="white", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Average Room Prices Per Night", x = "Price (Euros)", y = "Count")

#Correlation between numeric variables and room prices
reg_numeric <- hotel_df %>%
                select(where(is.numeric))   

corr_matrix <- cor(reg_numeric, use = "complete.obs")

#Generate correlation heatmap
corrplot::corrplot(corr_matrix,
                   method      = "color",
                   type        = "upper",
                   tl.col      = "black",
                   tl.cex      = 0.65,
                   addCoef.col = "black",
                   number.cex  = 0.5,
                   mar         = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
```

##Prepare regression data
```{r}
#Remove booking status due to data leakage
reg_data <- hotel_df %>%
  select(-c(booking_status)) %>%
  na.omit()

#Train/Test split 80/20
train_index <- createDataPartition(reg_data$avg_price_per_room, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_reg <- reg_data[train_index, ]
test_reg <- reg_data[-train_index, ]

#10-fold cross-validation
cv_ctrl <- trainControl(method      = "cv",
                        number      = 10,
                        verboseIter = FALSE)
```

##Linear Regression
```{r}
lm_model <- train(avg_price_per_room ~ .,
                  data       = train_reg,
                  method     = "lm",
                  trControl  = cv_ctrl,
                  preProcess = c("nzv"))   # removes near-zero variance columns
summary(lm_model)

lm_predicts <- predict(lm_model, test_reg)
lm_rmse <- RMSE(lm_predicts, test_reg$avg_price_per_room)
lm_mae  <- MAE(lm_predicts,  test_reg$avg_price_per_room)
lm_r2   <- R2(lm_predicts,   test_reg$avg_price_per_room)

#Identify significant coefficients
lm_coef <- summary(lm_model$finalModel)$coefficient
print(round(lm_coef[lm_coef[, 4] < 0.05, ], 4))

#Generate diagnostic plots
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(lm_model$finalModel, main = "Linear Regression diagnostics")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

##Ridge Regression
```{r}
#Convert training data into a matrix format
x_train <- model.matrix(avg_price_per_room ~ ., train_reg)[, -1]
y_train <- train_reg$avg_price_per_room

#Convert test data into matrix format
x_test  <- model.matrix(avg_price_per_room ~ ., test_reg)[, -1]
y_test <- test_reg$avg_price_per_room

#Fit ridge with cross-validation 
ridge_cv <- cv.glmnet(x_train, y_train, alpha = 0, nfolds = 10)

#Compute lambda value that gives minimum cross-validated error
ridge_lambda <- ridge_cv$lambda.min
print(ridge_lambda)

#Predict room prices on the test set using optimal lambda
ridge_pred <- predict(ridge_cv, s = ridge_lamba, newx = x_test)

#Compute RMSE, R^2, MAE
ridge_rmse <- RMSE(as.vector(ridge_pred), test_reg$avg_price_per_room)
ridge_r2 <- R2(as.vector(ridge_pred),   test_reg$avg_price_per_room)
ridge_mae <- MAE(as.vector(ridge_pred),  test_reg$avg_price_per_room)

#Create new data frame with actual and predicted prices
ridge_plot <- data.frame(
  Actual    = test_reg$avg_price_per_room,
  Predicted = as.vector(ridge_pred)
)

#Generate the ridge scatter plot
ggplot(ridge_plot, aes(x = Actual, y = Predicted)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, colour = "grey") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0,
              colour = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title    = "Ridge Regression: Predicted vs Actual Room Price",
       subtitle = paste0("RMSE = ", round(ridge_rmse, 2),
                         " | MAE = ",  round(ridge_mae, 2),
                         " | R² = ",   round(ridge_r2,  3)),
       x = "Actual Price (EUR)",
       y = "Predicted Price (EUR)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

##Lasso Regression
```{r}
#Fit Lasso with cross-validation 
lasso_cv <- cv.glmnet(x_train, y_train, alpha = 1, nfolds = 10)

#Compute lambda value
lasso_lambda <- lasso_cv$lambda.min
print(lasso_lambda)

#Predict room prices on test set with optimal lambda
lasso_pred <- predict(lasso_cv, s = lasso_lambda, newx = x_test)

#Compute RMSE, R^2, MAE
lasso_rmse <- RMSE(as.vector(lasso_pred), test_reg$avg_price_per_room)
lasso_r2   <- R2(as.vector(lasso_pred), test_reg$avg_price_per_room)
lasso_mae  <- MAE(as.vector(lasso_pred), test_reg$avg_price_per_room)

#Feature selection
lasso_coeffs <- coef(lasso_cv, s = lasso_lambda)
lasso_df    <- data.frame(
  Feature     = rownames(lasso_coeffs),
  Coefficient = round(as.numeric(lasso_coeffs), 4)
) %>%
  filter(Feature != "(Intercept)") %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(Coefficient)))

lasso_kept <- lasso_df %>% filter(Coefficient != 0)
lasso_removed <- lasso_df %>% filter(Coefficient == 0)

print(lasso_kept)
print(lasso_removed)

#Generate ranked features plot
ggplot(lasso_kept,
       aes(x = reorder(Feature, abs(Coefficient)),
           y = Coefficient,
           fill = Coefficient > 0)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("orange", "green"),
                    labels = c("Negative", "Positive")) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title    = "Lasso: Retained Feature Coefficients",
       subtitle = paste0("Optimal Lambda = ",
                         round(lasso_lambda, 5),
                         " | Features kept = ", nrow(lasso_kept),
                         " | Features removed = ", nrow(lasso_removed)),
       x    = NULL,
       y    = "Coefficient",
       fill = "Direction") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

#Create new data frame with actual and predicted prices
lasso_plot <- data.frame(Actual = y_test, Predicted = lasso_pred)
print(head(lasso_plot))
colnames(lasso_plot) <- c("Actual", "Predicted")

#Generate the lasso scatter plot
ggplot(lasso_plot, aes(x = Actual, y = Predicted)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "green") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0,
              color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Lasso Regression: Predicted vs Actual",
       subtitle = paste0("RMSE = ", round(lasso_rmse, 2),
                         " | MAE = ",  round(lasso_mae, 2),
                         " | R² = ",   round(lasso_r2,  3)),
       x = "Actual Price (EUR)", y = "Predicted Price (EUR)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

##Random Forest
```{r}
#Set cross-validation rules 
cv_ctrl_rf <- trainControl(method      = "cv",
                            number      = 10,
                            verboseIter = TRUE)   # shows fold progress

#Train random forest model with ranger
rf_model <- train(avg_price_per_room ~ .,
                  data      = train_reg,
                  method    = "ranger",
                  trControl = cv_ctrl_rf,
                  tuneGrid  = data.frame(
                    mtry          = c(3, 5, 7),
                    splitrule     = "variance",
                    min.node.size = 5),
                  num.trees  = 100,
                  importance = "impurity")

#Predict room prices
rf_pred <- predict(rf_model, test_reg)

#Compute RMSE, R^2, MAE
rf_rmse <- RMSE(rf_pred, test_reg$avg_price_per_room)
rf_r2   <- R2(rf_pred,   test_reg$avg_price_per_room)
rf_mae  <- MAE(rf_pred,  test_reg$avg_price_per_room)

print(rf_rmse)
print(rf_r2)
print(rf_mae)

#Variable importance
rf_impt <- varImp(rf_model)

#Generate variable importance plot
plot(rf_impt,
     top  = 15,
     main = "Random Forest: Variable Importance — Room Price Prediction")

ggplot(rf_impt$importance %>%
         tibble::rownames_to_column("Feature") %>%
         arrange(desc(Overall)) %>%
         head(15),
       aes(x = reorder(Feature, Overall), y = Overall)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "green", alpha = 0.85) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Random Forest: variable importance — room price",
       x     = NULL,
       y     = "Importance") +
  theme_minimal()

#Generate actual vs predicted scatter plot
rf_plot <- data.frame( Actual = test_reg$avg_price_per_room, Predicted = rf_pred)

ggplot(rf_plot, aes(x = Actual, y = Predicted)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, colour = "pink") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0,
              colour = "red", linetype = "dashed",
              linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title    = "Random Forest: Predicted vs Actual Room Price",
       subtitle = paste0("RMSE = ", round(rf_rmse, 2),
                         " | MAE = ", round(rf_mae,  2),
                         " | R² = ",  round(rf_r2,   3)),
       x = "Actual Price (EUR)",
       y = "Predicted Price (EUR)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

#Classification

##Install packages
```{r}
install.packages("MASS")
install.packages("e1071")
install.packages("pROC")
install.packages("kernlab")
```

##Load libraries
```{r}
library(MASS)       
library(e1071)      
library(pROC)   
library(kernlab)
```

##Load hotel reservations data
```{r}
Hotel_Reservations <- read_csv("Desktop/machine learning cw/datasets/Hotel Reservations.csv")
View(Hotel_Reservations)
```

##Preprocessing
```{r}
#Remove identifier columns
hotel_df <- dplyr::select(Hotel_Reservations,
                           -any_of(c("Booking_ID")))
#Convert into factor
hotel_df$booking_status <- as.factor(hotel_df$booking_status)

#Convert categorical columns into factors
cat_cols <- c("type_of_meal_plan", "room_type_reserved",
              "market_segment_type")

for (col in intersect(cat_cols, colnames(hotel_df))) {
  hotel_df[[col]] <- as.factor(hotel_df[[col]])
}

hotel_df$repeated_guest <- as.factor(hotel_df$repeated_guest)
hotel_df$required_car_parking_space <- as.factor(hotel_df$required_car_parking_space)
```

##Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
```{r}
#Find cancellation rate
cancel_rate <- round(mean(hotel_df$booking_status == "Canceled") * 100, 1)
print(cancel_rate)

#Cancellation by market segment
ggplot(hotel_df, aes(x = market_segment_type,
                     fill = booking_status)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill", alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("green", "orange"),
                    labels = c("Not Cancelled", "Cancelled")) +
  labs(title = "Cancellation Rate by Market Segment",
       x = "Market Segment",
       y = "Proportion",
       fill = "Booking Status") +
  theme_minimal()

#Cancellation by meal plan
ggplot(hotel_df, aes(x = type_of_meal_plan,
                     fill = booking_status)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill", alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("green", "orange"),
                    labels = c("Not Cancelled", "Cancelled")) +
  labs(title = "Cancellation Rate by Meal Plan",
       x = "Meal Plan", y = "Proportion",
       fill = "Booking Status") +
  theme_minimal()
```

##Prepare classification data
```{r}
class_data <- hotel_df

#Train/Test split 80/20
train_idx  <- createDataPartition(class_data$booking_status,
                                   p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_class  <- class_data[train_idx, ]
test_class   <- class_data[-train_idx, ]

#10-fold cross-validation
cv_ctrl_class <- trainControl(method = "cv",
                        number = 10,
                        classProbs = TRUE,
                        summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
                        verboseIter = FALSE)
```

##Logistic regression
```{r} 
lr_model <- train(booking_status ~ .,
                  data      = train_class,
                  method    = "glm",
                  family    = "binomial",
                  trControl = cv_ctrl_class,
                  metric    = "ROC")

lr_pred  <- predict(lr_model, test_class)
lr_prob  <- predict(lr_model, test_class, type = "prob")[, "Canceled"]
lr_cfm <- confusionMatrix(lr_pred, test_class$booking_status, positive = "Canceled")
print(lr_cfm)

#Generate predicted probability distribution
ggplot(data.frame(Prob = lr_prob,
                  Actual = test_class$booking_status),
       aes(x = Prob, fill = Actual)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("orange", "green")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, colour = "red",
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title    = "Logistic Regression: Predicted Cancellation Probability",
       subtitle = paste0("Accuracy = ",
                         round(lr_cfm$overall["Accuracy"] * 100, 2), "%"),
       x    = "Predicted Probability of Cancellation",
       y    = "Count",
       fill = "Actual status") +
  theme_minimal()
```

##K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN)
```{r} 
#5-fold cross validation due to computational constraints
cv_ctrl_fast <- trainControl(method          = "cv",
                              number          = 5,
                              classProbs      = TRUE,
                              summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
                              verboseIter     = TRUE)

knn_model <- train(booking_status ~ .,
                   data      = train_class,
                   method    = "knn",
                   trControl = cv_ctrl_fast,
                   metric    = "ROC",
                   tuneGrid  = expand.grid(k = c(5, 9, 15)))

knn_pred <- predict(knn_model, test_class)
knn_prob <- predict(knn_model, test_class,
                    type = "prob")[, "Canceled"]

knn_cfm  <- confusionMatrix(knn_pred,
                             test_class$booking_status,
                             positive = "Canceled")
print(knn_cfm)

#Generate ROC by k
plot(knn_model,
     main = "KNN: ROC by Number of Neighbours (k)")
```

##Support Vector Machine (SVM)
```{r} 
svm_model <- train(booking_status ~ .,
                   data       = train_class,
                   method     = "svmRadial",
                   trControl  = cv_ctrl_fast,
                   metric     = "ROC",
                   tuneLength = 3,              # reduced from 5
                   preProcess = c("center", "scale"))
print(svm_model)

svm_pred <- predict(svm_model, test_class)
svm_prob <- predict(svm_model, test_class,
                    type = "prob")[, "Canceled"]

svm_cfm  <- confusionMatrix(svm_pred,
                             test_class$booking_status,
                             positive = "Canceled")

print(svm_cfm)
```

##Random Forest
```{r} 
cv_ctrl_rf <- trainControl(method          = "cv",
                            number          = 10,
                            classProbs      = TRUE,
                            summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
                            verboseIter     = TRUE)

rf_model2 <- train(booking_status ~ .,
                  data      = train_class,
                  method    = "ranger",
                  trControl = cv_ctrl_rf,
                  metric    = "ROC",
                  tuneGrid  = data.frame(
                    mtry          = c(3, 5, 7),
                    splitrule     = "gini",
                    min.node.size = 5),
                  num.trees  = 100,
                  importance = "impurity")

rf_pred2  <- predict(rf_model2, test_class)
rf_prob2  <- predict(rf_model2, test_class,
                    type = "prob")[, "Canceled"]

rf_cfm   <- confusionMatrix(rf_pred2,
                             test_class$booking_status,
                             positive = "Canceled")

print(rf_cfm)

#Feature importance plot
rf_impt2 <- varImp(rf_model2)
plot(rf_impt2, top = 15,
     main = "Random Forest: Feature Importance — Cancellation")

ggplot(rf_impt2$importance %>%
         tibble::rownames_to_column("Feature") %>%
         arrange(desc(Overall)) %>%
         head(15),
       aes(x = reorder(Feature, Overall), y = Overall)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "purple", alpha = 0.8) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Random Forest: Feature Importance — Cancellation Prediction",
       x = NULL, y = "Importance") +
  theme_minimal()
```

##Compare models
```{r} 
# Store all confusion matrices in a named list
cfm_list <- list(
  "Logistic Regression" = lr_cfm,
  "KNN"                 = knn_cfm,
  "SVM"                 = svm_cfm,
  "Random Forest"       = rf_cfm
)

# Extract all metrics in one block
class_results <- data.frame(
  Model       = names(cfm_list),
  Accuracy    = round(sapply(cfm_list, function(x) x$overall["Accuracy"])    * 100, 2),
  Sensitivity = round(sapply(cfm_list, function(x) x$byClass["Sensitivity"]) * 100, 2),
  Specificity = round(sapply(cfm_list, function(x) x$byClass["Specificity"]) * 100, 2),
  F1          = round(sapply(cfm_list, function(x) x$byClass["F1"])          * 100, 2),
  row.names   = NULL
)

print(class_results)

#Find the best model
best_model <- class_results$Model[which.max(class_results$Accuracy)]

#Generate bar chart
ggplot(class_results,
       aes(x    = reorder(Model, Accuracy),
           y    = Accuracy,
           fill = Model == best_model)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(Accuracy, "%")),
            hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey", "pink")) +
  coord_flip() + ylim(0, 110) +
  labs(title = "Classification Model Comparison — Accuracy",
       x = NULL, y = "Accuracy (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

#ROC curves
roc_lr  <- roc(test_class$booking_status, lr_prob,
               levels = c("Not_Canceled", "Canceled"),
               quiet  = TRUE)
roc_knn <- roc(test_class$booking_status, knn_prob,
               levels = c("Not_Canceled", "Canceled"),
               quiet  = TRUE)
roc_svm <- roc(test_class$booking_status, svm_prob,
               levels = c("Not_Canceled", "Canceled"),
               quiet  = TRUE)
roc_rf  <- roc(test_class$booking_status, rf_prob2,
               levels = c("Not_Canceled", "Canceled"),
               quiet  = TRUE)

# Add AUC to results table
class_results$AUC <- round(c(auc(roc_lr),  auc(roc_knn),
                            auc(roc_svm), auc(roc_rf)), 3)
print(class_results)

#Best model by AUC
class_results[which.max(class_results$AUC), ]

# ROC curve plot — all four models
plot(roc_rf,  col = "purple", lwd = 2,
     main = "ROC Curves — all classification models")
plot(roc_lr,  col = "orange", lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
plot(roc_knn, col = "blue", lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
plot(roc_svm, col = "green", lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
abline(a = 0, b = 1, lty = 2, col = "gray")
legend("bottomright",
       legend = c(
         paste0("Random Forest (AUC = ", round(auc(roc_rf),  3), ")"),
         paste0("Logistic Reg  (AUC = ", round(auc(roc_lr),  3), ")"),
         paste0("KNN           (AUC = ", round(auc(roc_knn), 3), ")"),
         paste0("SVM           (AUC = ", round(auc(roc_svm), 3), ")")),
       col = c("purple", "orange", "blue", "green"),
       lwd = 2, cex = 0.8)

#Best confusion matrix
best_cfm <- switch(best_model,
                   "Logistic Regression" = lr_cfm,
                   "KNN"                 = knn_cfm,
                   "SVM"                 = svm_cfm,
                   "Random Forest"       = rf_cfm)
print(best_cfm)
```
